name: Clay
description: Clay GTM data from any AI agent: search Clay's people and company database, run Clay enrichment and custom functions, query Clay tables, search Workflow runs and check credits. Clay Public API with a personal API key.
instructions:
## Clay
This connector uses the Clay Public API (`https://api.clay.com/public/v0`): searches of Clay's people and company database, runs of Clay functions (enrichment and research), queries of Clay tables, Workflow run search, credit balance and privacy deletion.

What it cannot do: the Public API has no endpoints to list tables or functions, create tables or write rows. Rows are still written to tables through a table's inbound webhook, and function and table ids are copied from the Clay app.

**Setup**
1. In Clay open **API and CLI**, tab **API keys** (`https://app.clay.com/workspaces/~/api-and-cli?tab=api-keys`) and create a key. The key acts as your user, with your workspace access.
2. Paste it into `CLAY_API_KEY`. It is sent in the `clay-api-key` header.
3. For custom functions, open the function in Clay, **Details**, and enable **API** access; copy its `t_...` id.

**Check the key**: `clay_get_me` returns the user and workspace; `clay_get_credit_balance` shows the credits left.

**Search the GTM database**
1. `clay_get_search_query_reference` once per session to learn the fields and grammar.
2. `clay_create_search` with a query such as `select from companies where people.exists(is_current = true and job_title is_similar_to ("VP Sales"))`; keep the `search_id`.
3. `clay_get_search_results` with that id; it is a stateful iterator: each call returns the next page, call again while `has_more` is true.
Search results count against the plan's result limits (free: 50 per search and 100 per 30 days; paid: 500 per request). Over a limit Clay answers 402 naming the limit.

**Enrich with a function**
1. `clay_run_routine` with the routine id (`function:t_...`) and up to 100 items `{"id": "...", "inputs": {...}}`. It spends credits.
2. `clay_get_run_results` with the `routine_run_id`: HTTP 202 and `status: in_progress` while running, then 200 with `status: complete` and `data`. Match results to inputs by `id`, not by order; a complete run can contain failed items. `total` and `finished` count the whole run, `finished` includes failures. Poll every few seconds, not in a tight loop.
3. `clay_get_batch_run_results` reads batch runs started from the Clay CLI; a finished batch returns `result_url`.

**Tables (Enterprise)**: `clay_query_tables` with the table id from the table's URL (`.../tables/t_...`). Cells come back with a `status`: `success` (with `value`), `empty`, `error` (with `error`), or a pending state (`running`, `queued`, `retry`, `rate_limited`, `awaiting_callback`). Pass `cursor` back to page; a scan can return a row twice when it changes mid-scan, so deduplicate by id.

**Workflows (beta)**: `clay_get_runs_query_reference`, then `clay_query_workflow_runs` to find runs and their status.

**Privacy**: `clay_privacy_delete_people` (installed switched off) deletes people from Audiences; try `dry_run: true` first, then follow the job with `clay_get_privacy_deletion_status`.

**Paging**: collections return `data` and a `cursor` while more pages exist; search iterators return `data` and `has_more`.

**Errors**: errors carry a `message`. 401/403: wrong key or no access; 402: search result limit reached; 404: unknown id, or a function without API access; 409/422: invalid request state or input; 429: workspace rate limit, wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

CLAY_API_KEY.label: API key
CLAY_API_KEY.help: Clay: API and CLI, API keys, create a key. It acts with your user and workspace access.
CLAY_API_KEY.patternMessage: Paste only the API key, without spaces.

verifyHints.401: Clay refused the API key. Create a new one under API and CLI, API keys.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Clay limits requests per workspace. Wait for the time in Retry-After and try again.

tools.name: clay_get_me
tools.description: Get the Clay user and workspace the API key belongs to. Use it to check the key and to learn the workspace id.

tools.name: clay_get_credit_balance
tools.description: Get the current credit balances of the workspace. Reading balances costs no credits.

tools.name: clay_get_search_query_reference
tools.description: Get the reference of the Clay search query language (markdown): the queryable people and company fields, operators and grammar. Read it before writing a query for clay_create_search.

tools.name: clay_create_search
tools.description: Start a search of Clay's people or company database with a Clay search query, e.g. select from people where experiences.any(is_current = true and job_title is_similar_to ("VP Sales")). Returns a search_id; fetch the records with clay_get_search_results.

query.description: Clay search query, starting with "select from people" or "select from companies". Count queries and job searches are not supported.

tools.name: clay_get_search_results
tools.description: Fetch the next page of records of a search. Each call advances the search; call again while has_more is true. People come with name, location and matched experiences; companies with domain, industry, size, revenue and LinkedIn URL.

limit.description: Records in this page (default 20, at most 500 on paid plans, 50 on free and trial).

tools.name: clay_query_tables
tools.description: Read rows of known Clay tables (Enterprise plans) with selected fields, filters, ordering, grouping and joins. Returns rows with each cell's status and value, and a cursor for the next page.

query.description: Structured query: {"tables": [{"id": "t_0te9i4tZEHwc9hihBXu"}], "select": [{"field": "Company Name", "as": "company_name"}, {"field": "Domain"}], "filter": {"field": "Domain", "op": "is_not_empty"}, "order_by": [{"field": "Domain", "direction": "asc"}], "field_mode": "names"}. Filter ops: =, !=, >, >=, <, <=, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with, in, not_in, is_empty, is_not_empty; combine with {"and": [...]}, {"or": [...]}, {"not": {...}}. Up to 5 tables, 20 selected fields, 3 order_by entries (order_by disables cursor paging).

tools.name: clay_run_routine
tools.description: Run a Clay function (Clay-managed or a custom function with API access enabled) on 1 to 100 input items, for example to find work emails or enrich companies. Runs are asynchronous and spend Clay credits; poll clay_get_run_results with the returned routine_run_id.

routine_id.description: Routine id, e.g. function:t_abc123 for a custom function (the t_... id from the function details in Clay, prefixed with function:).

items.description: Inputs: [{"id": "row-1", "inputs": {"domain": "clay.com"}}]. id (at most 64 characters) is yours and comes back with the result; inputs are the function's input names.

webhook_id.description: Id of a registered Clay webhook to notify when the run finishes.

tools.name: clay_get_run_results
tools.description: Get the progress and results of a routine run. While it runs: HTTP 202 with total and finished counts. When done: status complete and data with one entry per input id, each complete with result or failed with error. Paged with cursor.

tools.name: clay_get_batch_run_results
tools.description: Get the progress of a batch routine run started from the Clay CLI or API, and when complete the download URL of its results file.

tools.name: clay_get_runs_query_reference
tools.description: Get the reference of the workflow-run query language (markdown): queryable run fields, node predicates, content search and grammar. Read it before clay_query_workflow_runs. Beta.

tools.name: clay_query_workflow_runs
tools.description: Search Clay Workflow runs with a run query: a select query returns matching runs newest first with a cursor, a count query returns the number of runs. Beta; data can lag a few seconds.

query.description: Run query in the grammar from clay_get_runs_query_reference (at most 2000 characters).

tools.name: clay_get_privacy_deletion_status
tools.description: Check a privacy deletion job from clay_privacy_delete_people, including its cascading cleanup. Status stays available up to five days after the job ends.

tools.name: clay_privacy_delete_people
tools.description: Delete people from Clay Audiences for a privacy request (for example a GDPR erasure), matched by email, LinkedIn slug or phone. Run with dry_run true first to see how many people match. Switched off by default.

person_identifiers.description: 1-100 identifiers; people matching any are deleted: {"type": "email", "value": "jane@example.com"}, {"type": "linkedin", "value": "jane-doe"} (the slug after /in/, not the URL) or {"type": "phone", "value": "+4915112345678"}.

dry_run.description: true only counts the matching people without deleting (default false).
